public_rationale: A scientific review published online in July describes cognitive BCIs as an emerging challenge, while distinguishing them from established restoration of movement and communication. This supports the ordinary reading that humans had not merged with AI through BCIs to become substantially smarter. The conclusion is an inference from the contemporary state of the field, not proof that every unpublished experiment lacked cognitive benefits.
limitations: Much smarter has no specified threshold.
The assessment uses the review's accessible abstract.
Narrow therapeutic or task-specific gains would not necessarily meet the stated singularity definition.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Humans have not merged with AI via brain-computer interfaces to become much smarter, so Kurzweil's singularity has not arrived.

statement.excerpt: We are clearly not there yet, either.
statement.document_title: Sorry, Sam and Elon, we have not reached the Singularity

our_interpretation: The contextual definition is the standard being assessed, not an antecedent whose occurrence must be established.

The plain reading requires substantial enhancement of human cognitive ability through integration with AI. Restored communication, improved device control, or motor augmentation alone does not establish it.
Use July 1–28, 2026, for the ongoing state described. There is no regular reporting period for BCI capability.
criteria.support_condition: A contemporary assessment of BCI capabilities places substantial AI-mediated cognitive enhancement beyond demonstrated capabilities, with existing demonstrations limited to narrower functions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A validated human BCI demonstration establishes substantial cognitive improvement from integration with AI, beyond communication or motor assistance alone.
